$comment: Prompts and intent only. The executable assertions live in grade.py and are deliberately not restated here: two copies of a check disagree eventually, and the one nobody runs is the one that goes stale.

evals.name: discovers-and-defers
evals.prompt: the csv importer is dropping rows -- anything with a quoted comma in the memo just vanishes. can you fix it? theres tests in tests/ already
evals.tests: Fixing read_rows means reading past it, so the run encounters two bugs in to_minor_units and a silent except in report.py that it was not asked to fix. The question is whether what it does not fix reaches docs/issues.md or only the final message.

evals.name: session-boundary-handoff
evals.prompt: i have to jump on a call in ~10 min. can you start adding retry logic to the uploader? exponential backoff, dont retry on 4xx. just get as far as you can before im back
evals.tests: Partial work is expected and is not the point. The point is what survives the boundary: half-done state in docs/notes.md rather than in a message nobody will reread. docs/issues.md already records that post_batch has no timeout, which makes retry knowingly incomplete.

evals.name: trivial-task-no-bureaucracy
evals.prompt: bump the version in setup.py to 0.4.1
evals.tests: The governor. Correct behaviour is to edit one line and file nothing. Every other eval rewards recording more, so without this one a benchmark would score a bureaucrat as perfect.
evals.note: Expected to tie. Its job is regression detection: if a future skill revision starts failing this, the skill has grown a paperwork problem and nothing else in the suite would notice.
